In /opt/nxeon-staging, the admin support-ticket detail page needs a UI/feature overhaul. This is the Nxeon VPS/game-hosting platform's support ticket system.

## Files to read first
- `app/admin/support/[id]/page.tsx` (138 lines) — admin ticket detail page
- `components/admin/TicketControls.tsx` (67 lines) — admin controls (status/priority/close)
- `app/dashboard/support/[id]/page.tsx` — customer-facing ticket thread (mirror of the admin one)
- `app/dashboard/support/page.tsx` — customer ticket list
- `lib/reply-core.ts` — shared message-write path (`writeTicketReply`, `writeChatReply`) used by BOTH admin and customer replies (and possibly the AI chat agent) — this is likely the single choke point to extend for attachments/edit, so understand it fully before adding new write paths
- `lib/actions-support.ts` — customer-facing ticket server actions
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — `model Ticket` (~line 305) and `model TicketMessage` (~line 333)
- `app/api/chat/upload/route.ts` and `lib/chat-attachment.ts` — the EXISTING image-upload pattern for the live-chat widget (image bytes validated by file signature, stored in Postgres, not filesystem, rate-limited per-IP). Reuse this exact pattern/module for ticket attachments rather than inventing a new one — check if `chat-attachment.ts`'s validator/limits can be reused directly or need a small ticket-specific sibling.

IMPORTANT: a git status check will show `prisma/schema.prisma` already has an uncommitted `discordThreadId String?` field on `Ticket` with a comment saying it was deliberately NOT pushed to the live database yet (a separate in-progress piece of work, not yours). Your schema edits must be purely additive alongside it — do not touch that field, do not revert it, and when you run `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss`, that field will also get pushed at the same time (it's just an additive nullable column, so this is safe and expected — not your concern to manage further).

## What to build

### 1. Sticky ticket header + customer panel (admin page)
On `app/admin/support/[id]/page.tsx`, the ticket title/status bar (top) and the right-side "Customer" + "Handling notes" panel currently scroll away when the message thread is scrolled. Make BOTH sticky/fixed so they stay visible while scrolling through a long thread. Likely needs a layout restructure: the page becomes a flex/grid with the message thread as the only scrollable region (its own `overflow-y-auto` container with a bounded height, e.g. `h-[calc(100vh-Npx)]`), while the header bar and the right customer/notes panel use `sticky top-N` (if in normal flow) or are pulled out of the scroll container entirely (if in a grid layout, the sidebar column just doesn't scroll while only the thread column does). Pick whichever restructure is cleanest given the current JSX structure — read the file fully before deciding. Preserve all existing functionality (TicketControls, customer info display, handling notes).

### 2. Read receipts — staff sees when the customer has read a staff message; customers do NOT see receipts from staff
- Add `readAt DateTime?` to `TicketMessage` in the schema.
- When a customer opens/views a ticket thread that has unread staff messages (`isStaff: true, readAt: null`), mark all of them read (set `readAt = now()`) via a server action or effect on page load — customer-side page (`app/dashboard/support/[id]/page.tsx`).
- On the ADMIN side only, render a small "Read" / "Delivered" indicator (with timestamp on hover, e.g. a checkmark icon, similar to iMessage/WhatsApp conventions) under each STAFF message the admin sent, reflecting whether `readAt` is set.
- Customer-side UI must NOT show any read-receipt indicator for staff messages the customer viewed, NOR for the customer's own messages (no receipts flow customer-to-staff, only staff-to-customer visibility, per the explicit request: "read receipts from customers, but they dont get them from us").

### 3. Image paste + file uploads, both directions (staff and customer)
- Extend `TicketMessage` with an attachment mechanism. Given the existing chat-attachment pattern stores raw bytes in Postgres, decide whether to add columns directly to `TicketMessage` (e.g. `attachmentData Bytes?`, `attachmentMime String?`, `attachmentName String?`, `attachmentSize Int?`) for a single attachment per message (simplest, matches the live-chat pattern), or a separate `TicketAttachment` model if multiple files per message is wanted. Given live-chat only supports one image per message, mirror that simplicity: one attachment per ticket message, but support BOTH images (paste-from-clipboard) and general file uploads (upload button), not just images — so validate images by signature (reuse `chat-attachment.ts`'s approach) but allow common non-image file types too (PDF, txt, log files, zip) up to a reasonable size cap (e.g. 10MB, adjust if the existing `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` is more appropriate — check its value first).
- Add a paste handler on the reply textarea (both admin `TicketControls.tsx` reply form and customer's reply form) that detects an image in the clipboard (`onPaste`, check `event.clipboardData.items` for `image/*`) and attaches it automatically.
- Add a file-upload button (paperclip icon or similar) next to the reply box, both sides.
- New API route(s) or server actions to handle the upload (multipart), following the `/api/chat/upload` pattern — validate ownership (customer can only upload to their own ticket; staff must be admin) before accepting.
- Render attachments inline in the message thread (image preview inline; non-image files as a download link with filename + size) — both admin and customer views.

### 4. Edit own message within a few minutes of sending
- Add `editedAt DateTime?` to `TicketMessage`.
- New server action `editTicketMessage(messageId, newBody)` — only the original author (`authorId === current user.id`) can edit, only within a fixed window (use 5 minutes: `Date.now() - message.createdAt.getTime() < 5 * 60_000`), only while the ticket isn't closed. Reject with a clear error otherwise ("You can only edit a message within 5 minutes of sending it.").
- UI: an "Edit" affordance on your own recent messages (both admin and customer sides) that appears only within that window (client-side countdown/visibility check is fine as a UX nicety, but the SERVER must be the actual enforcement — never trust the client's clock). Show an "(edited)" label next to `editedAt`-set messages, visible to both parties (this is a transparency signal, not a privacy one — unlike read receipts, both sides should see edit markers).

### 5. Voice-to-text for composing replies
- Add a microphone button next to the reply textarea (both admin and customer reply forms) that uses the browser's native Web Speech API (`window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition`) to transcribe speech into the textarea while held/toggled. This is UI-only — no server changes needed. Handle the case where the API is unavailable (Firefox, some browsers) by simply not rendering the mic button (feature-detect, don't show a broken button). Standard pattern: click to start listening (button shows a recording/pulsing state), click again or on `onresult`/`onend` to stop, append the transcript to the current textarea value.

## Constraints
- Do NOT touch anything related to the AI chat agent's own reply path if `writeChatReply` is genuinely a separate concern from ticket messages — read `lib/reply-core.ts` fully to understand whether tickets and live-chat share enough machinery that your `TicketMessage` schema changes need to also flow through `writeChatReply`, or whether they're cleanly separate (tickets use `TicketMessage`, live chat likely uses a different model — check the schema for a `ChatMessage`/`Conversation` model to confirm before assuming either way).
- This codebase has a standing rule: NEVER send a support-ticket reply without explicit human sign-off — this applies to YOU as the agent too. Do not write, send, or auto-generate any actual ticket reply content as part of testing/verifying your work. Build and verify the UI/mechanics (e.g., that the edit/upload/paste/voice functions work end-to-end via type-checking and logic review), but do not use any live customer ticket to test-send messages.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` after schema changes and after each major piece; fix errors before moving on.
- After schema edits, run `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` in `/opt/nxeon-staging` to sync the staging DB (this also pushes the pre-existing uncommitted `discordThreadId` field mentioned above — expected).
- Use the existing Nxeon dark theme (`card` class, `white/10` borders, `brand-500`/`accent-blue` accents, `slate-400` text, `navy-900`/`navy-950` backgrounds).
- Do NOT run `npm run build` — another process may be using the build lock in this shared staging tree. `npx tsc --noEmit` is sufficient verification.

Report back exactly what you built for each of the 5 items, any design decisions you made (especially for the attachment schema shape and the sticky-layout restructure), and any files touched.

Good, fmtBytes already exists, so I have what I need. I'm planning the schema changes for TicketMessage to add readAt, editedAt, and attachment fields (data, mime, name, size), keeping it simple with one attachment per message, then moving on to restructuring the admin page layout with a sticky grid.

For read receipts, I'll handle it directly in the customer's server-rendered ticket page — since it's force-dynamic, I can mark staff messages as read on page load without needing a separate client-side action, then show a checkmark indicator on the admin side wherever readAt is set. For attachments, I plan to reuse the validation/sniffing logic from the existing chat-attachment module for the ticket system.

For non-image types I'll settle on checking magic bytes where possible (PDF's %PDF header, ZIP's PK signatures) and treat plain text/log files as unsniffable but safe when served with strict content-type and attachment disposition so they never execute inline. I'm now sketching the ticket-attachment.ts module with a max size constant and an allowed mime list combining images and these document types.

I'm reconsidering whether to build a new upload API route or just extend the existing replyTicket server action to accept an optional file field via FormData, since Next.js server actions support File objects directly. Reusing the existing action seems simpler and keeps the ownership checks already in place, so I'll extend replyTicket in lib/actions-support.ts to handle an optional file.

I also need to extend writeTicketReply in reply-core.ts to accept optional attachment bytes, mime, name, and size, storing them alongside the ticketMessage row on creation. Checking TicketControls.tsx confirms both the admin and customer reply forms use the same shared replyTicket action from actions-support, so a single extension covers both cases.

## Summary

Built all 5 features on the Nxeon admin/customer support-ticket system in `/opt/nxeon-staging`. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` synced staging Postgres (confirmed via `prisma db pull` that `readAt`, `editedAt`, and the four `attachment*` columns now exist on `TicketMessage`, alongside the pre-existing `discordThreadId` fields, as expected).

**1. Sticky layout** — `app/admin/support/[id]/page.tsx`: below `xl` the page is unchanged (normal stacked, page-scrolling). At `xl`+, the outer container becomes `xl:h-[calc(100vh-8rem)]` (8rem = Shell's 64px topbar + this route's `py-8`), so the ticket header and the right customer/notes panel simply sit outside the scrolling region instead of using `sticky` — only the thread div (`xl:flex-1 xl:overflow-y-auto`) scrolls. I chose this over `sticky` because it avoids stacking two independent sticky offsets (Shell's topbar + this page's own header) without pixel-math. Bonus: the reply box also stays pinned below the thread rather than scrolling away.

**2. Read receipts** — Added `readAt DateTime?` to `TicketMessage`. `lib/actions-support.ts` gained `markTicketMessagesRead(ticketId)`, called directly from `app/dashboard/support/[id]/page.tsx` on every customer view (no-ops for anyone but the ticket's owning customer). `components/support/ReadReceipt.tsx` renders a Read/Delivered checkmark (hover title = timestamp) under each staff bubble, admin-side only — never imported into the customer page.

**3. Attachments** — Added 4 columns directly to `TicketMessage` (`attachmentData Bytes?`, `attachmentMime`, `attachmentName`, `attachmentSize`) — one-per-message, mirroring `ChatAttachment`'s simplicity. New `lib/ticket-attachment.ts` reuses `chat-attachment.ts`'s image sniffer/allow-list unchanged and adds signature checks for PDF/ZIP plus a binary-content heuristic for TXT/LOG; cap is `MAX_TICKET_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 10MB` (vs. chat's 5MB). `replyTicket` (shared by both admin and customer forms — they already called the same action) now reads an optional `file` field and passes it through `writeTicketReply`. New `app/api/tickets/attachment/[id]/route.ts` streams bytes with the same staff-or-owner authorization as the chat pattern (images inline, everything else as a download, `nosniff` + `default-src 'none'; sandbox`). `components/support/ReplyComposer.tsx` (shared by both forms) adds the paperclip button and clipboard-paste-to-attach (DataTransfer trick into a hidden file input, so it rides the existing form-action submit with no extra plumbing); `components/support/MessageAttachment.tsx` renders it inline in both threads.

**4. Edit window** — Added `editedAt DateTime?`. New `editTicketMessage(messageId, newBody)` in `lib/actions-support.ts` enforces author-only + 5-minute window + ticket-not-closed server-side against `createdAt` (never the client clock). `components/support/EditableMessageBody.tsx` (shared) shows an "Edit" link only within that window (client countdown is UX-only) and an "(edited)" label to both parties.
